title: Random forests link CT features to catheter-measured endpoints in CTEPH
summary: Random forests combined CT measurements and qualitative findings to classify catheter-measured hemodynamic endpoints in patients with operable chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension. Retrospective internal testing reported AUC 0.82 for a pulmonary-pressure category and 0.74 for a pulmonary-artery oxygen-saturation category. Replacement of invasive testing or improved management was not demonstrated.
organization: Technical University of Munich; Saarland University Medical Center; University Hospital Schleswig-Holstein; Robert Bosch Hospital

source_review.scope: Read primary cohort/reference, CT-feature assessment, normalization/random-forest evaluation Methods, endpoint Results and limitations. Actual source describes threefold random sampling; a more detailed nested validation design is not inferred. Exact primary identity/date and fresh primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Single-center retrospective cohort of 127 operable CTEPH patients from 2015–2020 with CT and preoperative right-heart catheterization. Pulmonary pressure was available in 127 patients and pulmonary-artery oxygen saturation in 55. Random forests used normalized quantitative and qualitative CT features, evaluated through a source-described threefold random-sampling procedure. Reported endpoint-classification AUCs were 0.82 and 0.74.
evidence.unknown: Small selected surgical cohort, including only 55 patients for the oxygen endpoint; no external model validation. Exact normalization/filtering nesting and hyperparameter selection were incompletely specified. CT-feature associations are observational, and feature importance is not causation. Benefits for patient management and replacement of catheterization remain untested.
evidence.ai_role: Random forests learned combinations of CT-derived measurements and qualitative imaging findings to classify catheter-referenced hemodynamic categories; feature filtering characterized the model-relevant signals.
